product.reading: Reading the storage and the targets.

functions.title: Top functions
functions.description: By self time: the value spent in the function itself, wherever it is called from.
functions.selfDetail: Share of the whole spent in the function itself, not in what it calls.
functions.totalDetail: Share of the whole spent in the function and in what it calls.

profilesPage.title: Profiles
profilesPage.description: Every service with profiles, and what was read from the pull targets. Profiles are kept {{days}} days.
profilesPage.cpuDetail: Cores used on average, from the CPU profiles

services.title: Services
services.description: Each service and the profile types it has in the range.
services.viaDetail: Pushed by Grafana Alloy or an SDK, or pulled by Profiling from a target's pprof address.
services.noneDetail: Run Grafana Alloy's eBPF profiler on your hosts, add the Pyroscope SDK to a service, or add a pull target.

captures.title: Captures
captures.description: Profiles read from the pull targets, newest first
captures.noneDetail: Pull targets are read on their schedule, and whenever someone captures a profile now.

capture.title: Capture a profile now
capture.description: Reads one profile from a pull target now and stores it. Its row in Captures says when it is stored, or why not.
capture.noTargets: Add a pull target first, under Targets.
capture.cpuTakes: A CPU profile samples the service for {{seconds}} seconds.

flamePage.title: Flame graphs
flamePage.description: Where time and memory go, function by function. Width is the share of the whole; click a frame to zoom in.
flamePage.noneDetail: Profiles arrive from Grafana Alloy's eBPF profiler, the Pyroscope SDKs, or the pull targets Profiling reads.
flamePage.failed: The flame graph could not be read
flamePage.graphDetail: Width is the share of the whole · hover a frame for its numbers · click to zoom
flamePage.pick: Pick a service and a profile type
flamePage.emptyDetail: The service has no profiles of this type in the range. Pick a longer range, or another type.

comparePage.title: Compare
comparePage.description: Where the time moved between two periods, or between two versions in the same period. Shares of the whole are compared, so a busier period does not make every function look slower.

baseline.day: The same period a day before
baseline.week: The same period a week before

comparePage.noLabelsDetail: The service's profiles have no labels in this range, such as version. Compare two periods instead.
comparePage.pickTwoDetail: Baseline and comparison are both {{name}} {{value}}. Choose another value to see what changed.
comparePage.failed: The comparison could not be read
comparePage.missingBase: {{name}} has no profiles of this type. Pick another baseline.
comparePage.missingHead: {{name}} has no profiles of this type. Pick a longer range.
comparePage.changeDetail: Difference in the share of the whole spent in the function itself, in percentage points. Above 0 it takes more than it did.

targets.title: Pull targets
targets.description: Services that serve pprof over HTTP, such as Go's net/http/pprof. Profiling reads them on a schedule, or when someone captures a profile now.
targets.addDetail: Each profile type is read at its path under the address: /profile?seconds=N for CPU, /heap, /goroutine, /mutex and /block.
targets.deleteDetail: It is not read from now on. The profiles already read are kept for the retention.
targets.serviceHint: The name its profiles are stored under.
targets.urlHint: An address without a path reads /debug/pprof.
targets.labelsHint: name=value, one per line, added to every profile read, such as version or env.
targets.kept: Kept; leave empty to keep it
targets.sealed: Sealed with the install's key and never shown again.
targets.noneDetail: Services that push their profiles need none. Add one for a service that serves pprof.

setupPage.title: Setup
setupPage.description: How profiles reach Profiling, and how Grafana reads them. Pushing needs PROFILING_INGEST_TOKEN or an API token with the editor role.
setupPage.ebpfDetail: Every process on a Linux host or Kubernetes node, sampled with eBPF, with no change to the code. Alloy needs a recent kernel and runs privileged.
setupPage.sdkDetail: From inside a service, for Go, Java, Python, Ruby, .NET, Node.js and Rust, with heap and lock profiles and labels of your own.
setupPage.pullDetail: A service that serves pprof needs nothing installed: Profiling reads it.
setupPage.grafanaDetail: Grafana's Pyroscope data source reads Profiling as it would read Pyroscope, with an API token of the viewer role.

settingsPage.askAnAdmin: Ask an admin of this Profiling.

account.title: Account
account.description: Your profile, password, two-step verification and where you are signed in.

members.title: Members
members.description: Who can sign in to this Profiling, and with which role. Viewers see every profile; editors also capture profiles and push them; admins also keep pull targets, and manage members and tokens.

signin.title: Sign-in
signin.description: Identity providers people can sign in with, such as OpenAsy Identity, Keycloak or Microsoft Entra ID, and which of their groups give which role.

tokens.title: API tokens
tokens.description: For Grafana, Alloy, scripts and CI. Each token has one role and an expiry; the secret is shown once.

attention.storageDetail: Pyroscope, which keeps the profiles inside this container, does not answer. Nothing is stored or read until it does; Profiling starts it again on its own. Its logs are in the container's.
attention.disk: Only {{free}} free on the data volume
attention.diskDetail: Give the volume more space or keep profiles for fewer days (PROFILING_RETENTION_DAYS).
